explanations.answer: So the bodies won't stay up on the Sabbath
explanations.explanation: That's the reason the writer gives. The next day was a High Sabbath, so the Jews asked Pilate, the Roman governor, to have the legs broken and the bodies taken down. The text says the point was that the bodies would not remain on the cross during the Sabbath.

explanations.answer: So the soldiers can leave before dark
explanations.explanation: I get why that sounds like a reasonable guess. But the text never says anything about the soldiers' schedule. It says the Jews asked Pilate, the Roman governor, so that the bodies would not remain on the cross during the Sabbath. The Sabbath is the reason on the page.

explanations.answer: So the crowd will stop gathering there
explanations.explanation: No crowd control in this verse, friend. The text doesn't mention a crowd at all here. It says the Jews asked Pilate, the Roman governor, to have the legs broken and the bodies removed so they would not remain on the cross during the Sabbath. Stick with what the writer gives us.

I see why you stopped at one, because the verse is short and moves fast. But it says the soldiers broke the legs of the first man crucified with Jesus, and those of the other. That's both men, not one.
That's right, baker! John 19:32 says the soldiers broke the legs of the first man who had been crucified with Jesus, and those of the other. So both men got the same treatment.

explanations.answer: No because He is already dead
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. When the soldiers came to Jesus, they saw that He was already dead, so they did not break His legs. The writer gives that exact reason in the verse. Sometimes the text just hands you the answer, and I take those.

You've got the no, and that part is right. But Pilate doesn't step in anywhere in this verse. The text says the soldiers came to Jesus and saw that He was already dead, and that's why they did not break His legs.

explanations.answer: Yes just like the other two men
explanations.explanation: I understand the pattern, since the soldiers had just done the first man and then the other. But the pattern stops at Jesus. The text says they saw He was already dead, so they did not break His legs. I think that's the part of this passage that matters most.

That's the reason the writer gives. He says the one who saw it knows he is telling the truth, so that you also may believe. Notice the 'you' there. The writer is talking straight to whoever is reading.

explanations.answer: So readers will blame the soldier
explanations.explanation: Nothing in the text points the finger at the soldier. The writer says the one who saw it testified, and gives the reason: so that you also may believe. The soldier gets one verse, and blame isn't in it. I'd keep the focus where the writer puts it.
Pilate has his part in this passage, but fear isn't it. The one who saw it testified so that you also may believe. That's the writer's own reason, and it's about the reader, not the governor.

Right, baker. The writer says these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled, and then he quotes: “Not one of His bones will be broken.” That's the soldiers not breaking Jesus' legs. He wants us to see the Scripture and the cross lining up.

That's a fair guess, because the scene is rough and fast. But the text says the opposite. John 19:36 says these things happened “…so that the Scripture would be fulfilled…” and then gives the words: “Not one of His bones will be broken.” The writer says outright that the Scripture is the reason these things happened.

That's it. The writer says another Scripture says, “They will look on the One they have pierced.” The prophet Zechariah wrote those words (Zechariah 12:10). The spear in this passage is why the writer brings it up.

I get the thought, since the cross is a heavy scene. But the Scripture says something else: “They will look on the One they have pierced.” Zechariah, the prophet, wrote it (Zechariah 12:10). The word is look, not forget.

Hiding does show up in this passage, but it's not in this Scripture. The prophet Zechariah wrote, “They will look on the One they have pierced.” (Zechariah 12:10) The verb is look. I think the writer wants us to keep our eyes on Jesus here.

You've got it, baker. John 19:38 says Joseph of Arimathea was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews. That's the text's own reason. Keeping a secret is hard work, and I should know, because I once hid a burnt batch under a dish towel.

I see why you'd think so, since Pilate was a Roman and Joseph goes to him. But the text names a different group. It says Joseph was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews. Joseph asked Pilate for the body anyway, and that's what the text shows us.

Samaritans don't come up in this passage at all, friend. John 19:38 says Joseph of Arimathea was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews. When the text names the group, we take its word for it.

I see why you'd expect a no. But John 19:38 says Pilate gave permission, so Joseph came and removed the body. Joseph asked, and he got a yes. After all that hiding, I think that's a good moment for him.
That's right, baker. Joseph of Arimathea asked Pilate, and Pilate gave him permission. Then Joseph came and removed the body of Jesus. I bet asking took some nerve, but the answer was yes.

explanations.answer: To wrap the body for burial
explanations.explanation: That's right. The text says they took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices. Nicodemus, a Pharisee who had come to Jesus at night (John 3:1-2), brought the myrrh and aloes. It was a burial, and the spices went with the cloths.

explanations.answer: To pay the soldiers at the cross
explanations.explanation: Nothing in the text has the spices going to the soldiers. It says Joseph and Nicodemus took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices. The spices went with the burial cloths.

explanations.answer: To burn as an offering at the temple
explanations.explanation: Nothing in this passage goes near the temple. John 19:40 says they took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices. The myrrh and aloes were for the burial, right there with the body.

You got it, baker. John 19:40 says they wrapped the body in linen cloths with the spices, according to the Jewish burial custom. The writer tells us they did it the way it was done. It was careful work.

That's a fair guess if you thought they were in a hurry. But the text says they wrapped the body in linen cloths with the spices, according to the Jewish burial custom. So they did follow the custom. I think they took real care.

explanations.answer: A new tomb where no one had been laid
explanations.explanation: That's right. John 19:41 says that in the garden was a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid. Nobody had used it before. That's the tomb the writer points to.

explanations.answer: The tomb where Lazarus had been buried
explanations.explanation: Lazarus is a good name to think of. Jesus called him “our friend” (John 11:11), and Jesus called him out of his tomb (John 11:43-44). But this garden has a different tomb, a new one in which no one had yet been laid. I think the writer wants us to notice that nobody had been in it.

explanations.answer: The pool where a lame man had waited
explanations.explanation: That pool shows up earlier in John, in chapter 5 (John 5:2-9). But the garden here has something different. The text says there was a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid. That's a good memory, friend.

explanations.answer: It is the day of Preparation and the tomb is nearby
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. John 19:42 says they placed Jesus there because it was the Jewish day of Preparation and the tomb was nearby. Those are the two reasons the text gives. Sometimes the best place is the one that's close.

explanations.answer: Jesus had asked to be buried in that garden
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say Jesus asked for that. It gives different reasons: it was the Jewish day of Preparation, and the tomb was nearby. I'm not going to add a request the writer left out.

explanations.answer: Pilate had ordered that He be buried there
explanations.explanation: Pilate did have a part in this scene. He gave Joseph permission to remove the body (John 19:38). But the text never says he ordered the tomb. It says they placed Jesus there because it was the Jewish day of Preparation and the tomb was nearby.
